subject.title: fix(gateway): held-button retarget guard never fires when tools.invoke rebuilds the computer tool per call

question: Must this computer-control safety fix show a real paired-node Gateway run, or is the current engine-level run with mocked node discovery and dispatch sufficient?
rationale: The implementation and focused tests appear sound, but repository policy makes after-fix real behavior proof a merge gate for an external PR and the contributor explicitly could not exercise the relevant transport topology.

options.title: Require paired-node proof
options.body: Hold merge until a redacted real HTTP or RPC transcript or recording shows hold, blocked retarget, release, and successful recovery across two paired macOS nodes.

options.title: Accept engine proof
options.body: Treat the real invocation-engine output plus mocked node wire as sufficient and accept the remaining transport and long-running lifecycle uncertainty.

recommendation.title: Require paired-node proof
recommendation.body: Hold merge until a redacted real HTTP or RPC transcript or recording shows hold, blocked retarget, release, and successful recovery across two paired macOS nodes.

likelyOwner.reason: The original held-input safety invariant and surrounding computer-control lifecycle were introduced in the merged hardening commit associated with this path.
